fields.statement: QA cycle 1 with a fresh scratch build (go build -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza) in a scratch Rhiza root: rhiza run start --foreground on a gate step with commands [true-ish, 5000 lines + stderr + exit 3, touch marker] failed with the detail 'command 2 `...`: exit 3; full output: <run dir>/gate-gate-1-2.log' (5002 lines, stderr included), the third command still ran, and all ran in the run's worktree; an all-green gate passed. rhiza workflow check refused no commands, commands = [], a blank command, and prompt, agent and models on a gate, and commands on a command step. Broken: a gate step in an included workflow (outer [step.sub] kind = workflow, workflow = inner, inner gate ig) failed with 'its output could not be kept': the step name inner/ig makes gate-inner/ig-1-1.log a path under a directory that is never created. Scoped tests TestGateStep (workflow, run) pass.

QA cycle 1, scratch build, fake rex/claude shims: workflow agent build -> command check with on.fail = handback:build and no handback_cap; check red every time: the agent session was resumed 3 times (same session ID), the journal held 3 handback entries, and the 4th red parked the run stopped; rhiza inbox showed a handback item naming step check and the cause ('went fail after 3 hand-backs to build: exit 1 / tests red 4') with next rhiza run resume. Resume re-parked on red, then succeeded on green. handback_cap = 1 parked after one hand-back. A hand-back inside an included workflow (ihb/check -> ihb/build) works. workflow check refused handback_cap 0, -2, "3", 2.5, handback:nope, handback:check (a command step) and handback: with the step named.

QA cycle 1, scratch build: the resumed agent session read handback.md: for a red command step it named `check` and the output tail 'tests red 3'; for a red gate step it named `check` with 'output in <run dir>/gate-gate-1-2.log'. Each resume carried the step's handback text ('Fix it, see <session dir>/handback.md') with claude --resume and the same session ID. A session whose transcript is gone failed the step with 'session <id> cannot be resumed: no transcript ...'; an agent step with no handback template failed it naming the step and session. Scoped tests TestHandbackDeliver and TestScripts/run-handback pass.

QA cycle 1, scratch build: outside a run, rhiza run spawn exits 2 naming RHIZA_RUN; from an agent step's session, rhiza run spawn --role verifier --leaf myleaf --model opus --brief <file> --json started a child in the run's worktree (argv had --model opus and --permission-mode manual), wrote spawn/<sid>/brief.md as '## Contract' section then '## Brief' with the caller's file, journaled spawn then spawn-ended under step build, and printed outcome pass, detail exit 0, exit 0; a child exiting 7 gave outcome fail, detail exit 7, exit 1; a missing --brief nope.md exits 2 naming the path. With machine_hold in daemon.state.json the spawn journaled spawn-held 'machine hold: load 99 over 8', and once the state was cleared it started the child and reported held true. Scoped tests TestRunSpawn and TestScripts/run-spawn, describe-golden pass.

QA cycle 1, scratch build: with a spawned child blocked on a fifo, kill -9 of the foreground driver only (the spawn process lived on), then rhiza run resume --foreground: the driver reattached, waited on the step, and after the child was released the journal held exactly one spawn-ended (the spawn process and the driver did not both record it) and the run finished from step build. Scoped test TestSpawnResume passes.

QA cycle 1, scratch build: rhiza run status listed '## Spawned sessions' with '- build, verifier on myleaf, model opus, session <id>: ended, pass', a failed child as 'ended, fail (exit 7)' and a live one as 'running'; --json spawned[] carried step, parent, session, role, leaf, model, state, outcome, detail; rhiza session show <child id> shows the child's record. The web page and pane/message were exercised only through the scoped tests TestRunDetailSpawned, TestRunStatusSpawned and TestSpawnedSessionOpenResume, which pass (no daemon or Rex in the scratch setup).
